A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniR research, with matching authors, method and shared experiments. All pages, including appendices, are readable, and the equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical reasoning, translation, model-transfer, visual-math and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds medical prediction, multilingual evaluation, comparator experiments and diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: The core GRPO-trained reasoning module, additive logit guidance and omission of UniR's KL penalty remain unchanged. v3 adds optional CoS speculative decoding and EVA alignment for guidance across different tokenizers (Appendices B.3.3 and D.2). These extend inference procedures without replacing the central method.

E1.justification: v3 adds MIMIC-IV readmission and length-of-stay training/evaluation, transfer to mortality prediction, and MGSM problems answered in Japanese and Spanish. These substantially broaden domains, tasks and language conditions. MathVerse and Geometry3k are retained from v1 Appendix C.1, rather than newly introduced.

E2.justification: v3 evaluates Reasoning Vectors and RAST against UniR in Table 11, adding directly relevant methodological alternatives absent from v1. Table 18 also introduces a standalone distilled DeepSeek reasoner comparison. The size-ablation comparison drops GRPO Full, GRPO LoRA and the untrained 1.5B ensemble rows from v1 Table 5, although these comparisons appear elsewhere.

E3.justification: Primary evaluation changes from deterministic decoding to temperature 0.6, with greedy results retained in Appendix G. The main Qwen setting promotes the 1.5B module already evaluated in v1's appendix. New protocols include a 7B training backbone, cross-tokenizer controls, distilled-reasoner initialization, medical accuracy/F1 evaluation and latency measurement over 100 generated tokens.

E4.justification: v3 adds temperature sensitivity, reward-score separation before/after training, gradient-norm diagnostics, cross-tokenizer robustness, standalone 1.5B-module controls, pretrained-reasoner initialization and failure-case analyses. Existing size and training-dynamics analyses are retained or extended. New medical examples and semantic-error cases expand qualitative analysis, while v1's Russell example in Figure 15 is removed.

E5.justification: v1 reports deterministic benchmark point estimates and training reward-variation curves. v3 specifies ten evaluation runs with seeds 1–10 and reports means and standard deviations for Tables 1, 2 and 15. Figure 5 adds significance annotations at p < 0.001, although the test is unspecified. These additions establish evaluation uncertainty reporting, not independent training replications.

E6.justification: Many greedy results remain unchanged: Qwen with a 1.5B module averages 43.9 in both v1 Table 5 and v3 Table 16. New stochastic results report 42.7 for UniR versus 40.3 for GRPO Full, under different decoding conditions. v3 adds medical, multilingual, cross-tokenizer, efficiency and diagnostic results; the earlier greedy 0.5B comparison rows are omitted. The revised headline scores therefore do not establish same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: v1 provides an informal soft-Q theorem and short proof. v3 adds Appendix A's reward-equivalence lemma and proof, token-decomposition corollary, and expanded optimal-policy derivation, alongside a multi-objective KL derivation in Section 4.1. The soft-Q interpretation is retained but its formal treatment expands substantially; convergence to the required optimum remains assumed.

C1.justification: v3 narrows the claim of compatibility with any frozen LLM to shared or aligned token spaces and emphasizes within-family weak-to-strong transfer. It broadens headline contributions to medical/domain generalization and robustness under stochastic decoding. The abstract also removes v1's Llama-specific qualification on outperforming fine-tuning methods, changing the scope of the performance claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations linking sampling robustness to preserved backbone diversity, translation guidance to English-language reasoning, and pretrained reasoners to implicit rewards. It discusses medical accuracy/F1 tradeoffs and semantic failures. New limitations address tokenizer mismatch, conflicting module rewards and clinical applicability; the cross-tokenizer shortfall is attributed to imperfect alignment. These go beyond relocating v1's limitations.

D1.justification: v3 documents medical labels, prompts, context lengths, generation-group size and composition weights; language-prompt adaptations; and the CoS timing procedure. Appendix D supplies alignment and comparator implementation descriptions, including the Reasoning Vectors scaling factor. PhysioNet access is documented. Existing math/translation training details and the code link largely persist, but medical cohort sizes and splits remain unspecified.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially repositions UniR around modular guidance, adding TART, Reasoning Vectors and RAST and distinguishing their mechanisms. New connections cover endogenous rewards, tokenizer alignment, speculative decoding and broader RLVR applications. Earlier discussion and citations concerning Best-of-N, MCTS and RAIN are removed. This changes research positioning beyond citation-format updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, related work, theoretical interpretation and experiment narrative are substantially rewritten. Separate main-text efficiency and training-dynamics sections move into focused appendices, while visual-math evaluation moves into the main text. Experimental settings, limitations, prompts and qualitative examples are reorganized into a substantially different appendix structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. v1's visual-math Table 4 becomes v3 Figure 4 with unchanged scores; training plots move to the appendix. The standalone-performance figure gains a third panel, and new boxplots, comparison tables, medical examples and failure displays substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens assessment of the central empirical claims through seeded stochastic evaluation, retained greedy controls, relevant guidance baselines and targeted robustness analyses. Tokenizer qualifications and failure cases also better delimit applicability than v1's broad universal claims. Medical reproducibility remains incomplete, and the expanded optimality argument still assumes convergence. Nevertheless, the improved uncertainty reporting and direct tests of robustness and transfer address important weaknesses in v1's evidence.
